report:
**Conclusion**
Yes, denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in individuals with osteoporosis.

**Evidence and Key Findings**
* **Primary Clinical Evidence:** In the landmark 3-year FREEDOM trial, subcutaneous denosumab (60 mg administered every 6 months) reduced the relative risk of new morphometric vertebral fractures by **68%** compared to placebo in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. It also significantly reduced hip and non-vertebral fractures while increasing bone mineral density (BMD).
* **Long-Term Efficacy:** Long-term extension studies following patients for up to 10 years demonstrated that denosumab maintains low vertebral fracture rates and delivers progressive, non-plateauing increases in BMD over time. 
* **Systematic Reviews:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses consistently support denosumab as a highly effective anti-resorptive treatment for reducing new and worsening vertebral fractures. Clinical guidelines emphasize that because stopping denosumab leads to a rapid rebound in bone turnover, ongoing therapy or transition to another agent is necessary to maintain fracture prevention.

**Sources**
* New England Journal of Medicine (FREEDOM Trial): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
* Journal of Bone and Mineral Research (FREEDOM Analysis): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3415619/
* The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology (10-Year Extension Data): https://www.thelancet.com/journals/landia/article/PIIS2213-8587(17)30138-9/fulltext
* Reumatología Clínica / ScienceDirect Systematic Review: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1699258X12001787
